title: Tacos al Pastor
description: Thin pork slices marinated in a toasted guajillo-achiote adobo with pineapple, seared hot until charred at the edges and piled onto warm corn tortillas.

ingredients.item: dried guajillo chiles, stemmed and seeded
ingredients.note: or order dried guajillo online from a Mexican-goods importer; in a pinch use 2 tbsp mild chili powder plus 1 tsp smoked paprika

ingredients.item: dried ancho chile, stemmed and seeded
ingredients.note: if unavailable, add one extra guajillo instead
look for achiote paste at a Mexican grocer, or mix 2 tbsp atsuete/annatto powder with a little oil and vinegar
regular dried oregano works if Mexican oregano isn't available
to taste

steps: Toast the guajillo and ancho chiles in a dry pan for about 30 seconds per side, then soak them in hot water for 15 minutes until soft.
Blend the soaked chiles with the achiote paste, pineapple juice, vinegar, garlic, oregano, cumin, and salt until smooth.
Coat the pork slices in the adobo, cover, and marinate in the fridge for at least 2 hours, ideally overnight.
Heat a griddle or heavy skillet until very hot and sear the pork in batches for 2-3 minutes per side until charred at the edges and cooked through.
Chop the seared pork into small pieces and toss with the chopped pineapple.
Warm the tortillas on the same hot pan for about 20 seconds per side.
Fill the tortillas with the pork and pineapple, then top with onion, cilantro, and salsa.
tips: Marinate at least 2 hours, ideally overnight — that unattended time isn't counted in the cook time above.
A very hot, uncrowded pan matters more than a spit; crowded meat steams instead of charring.
kidNote: Blend the marinade without any extra chile de árbol and keep the table salsa off the kids' plates — they still get the smoky achiote and pineapple flavour without the heat. Put the arbol salsa on the table for the adults to add themselves.
nutritionNote: Rich in protein with moderate fat from the pork's natural marbling; balance the plate with the pineapple, shredded cabbage, or a simple salad.

title: Tacos de Carnitas
description: Pork shoulder simmered low and slow in its own fat with citrus, garlic, and spices until fork-tender, then crisped in the pan for tacos with soft and crackly bits in every bite.

ingredients.item: pork shoulder, cut into large chunks

ingredients.note: use vegetable oil if lard isn't available
to taste
to taste
to taste

steps: Season the pork chunks generously with salt, pepper, oregano, and cumin.
Place the pork in a heavy pot with the garlic, onion, orange halves, bay leaves, and lard, and add just enough water to almost cover the meat.
Simmer uncovered over low heat for about 2 hours, stirring occasionally, until the pork is fork-tender and the liquid has mostly evaporated.
Let the fat render out and fry the pork in it for the last 15-20 minutes, turning occasionally, until the edges turn crisp and golden.
Discard the orange halves and bay leaves, then shred the pork with two forks, keeping some of the crispy pieces whole.
Warm the tortillas on a hot dry pan for about 20 seconds per side.
Fill the tortillas with the pork and top with chopped onion, cilantro, and salsa verde.
tips: Resist covering the pot — the liquid needs to evaporate so the meat can fry in its own rendered fat.
Leftover carnitas keep refrigerated for 3 days and reheat crisp in a dry skillet.
nutritionNote: High in protein and rendered fat; serve with a squeeze of lime and a crunchy cabbage or radish salad to lighten the plate.

title: Elote
description: Grilled corn on the cob brushed with butter and lime-mayo crema, then coated in crumbled cotija and chile powder — the classic corn-on-a-stick from every market and plaza.

ingredients.note: use a mild paprika instead if serving young kids, and keep the spicier version for the adults
or finely crumbled salted white cheese, moistened slightly with a splash of milk

steps: Grill or boil the corn until tender and bright yellow, about 5-8 minutes, then let it cool slightly.
Whisk together the mayonnaise, lime juice, garlic, and half the chili powder in a small bowl.
Brush each ear of corn all over with melted butter.
Slather the corn generously with the mayo mixture using a brush or the back of a spoon.
Sprinkle each ear with cotija cheese, the remaining chili powder, and cilantro.
Serve immediately with lime wedges on the side.
tips: Grilling gives a smokier flavour than boiling, but boiled corn is faster for a weeknight snack.
Keep extra chili powder on the table so everyone can add their own heat.
nutritionNote: A fibre-rich vegetable side that turns rich with mayo and cheese; use a light hand on both if it's a side to a heavier main.

title: Esquites
description: Corn kernels simmered in butter with epazote and a whole serrano chile, spooned into cups with mayo, cotija, chile, and lime — the cup version of elote sold from market carts.

ingredients.note: frozen sweet corn kernels work well if fresh corn is out of season
epazote is hard to find in Manila — substitute a few cilantro sprigs, or leave it out entirely
or finely crumbled salted white cheese

ingredients.item: chili powder or ground chile de árbol
ingredients.note: to taste

steps: Melt the butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat and cook the onion until translucent, about 3 minutes.
Add the corn kernels, whole serrano chile, epazote, water, and salt.
Cook uncovered, stirring occasionally, for 8-10 minutes until the corn is tender and most of the liquid has evaporated.
Remove and discard the serrano chile and epazote sprigs.
Spoon the corn into cups or bowls and stir in a spoonful of mayonnaise per serving.
Top each cup with cotija cheese, a dusting of chili powder, and a squeeze of lime.
tips: Leaving the serrano whole infuses gentle heat without making the dish actually hot — pull it out before serving the kids' portions.
Char a handful of extra corn kernels in a dry pan first for a smokier, more market-stall flavour.
nutritionNote: A fibre-rich vegetable dish that turns rich with mayo and cheese; use a light hand on both if serving alongside a heavier main.

title: Sopes de Chorizo
description: Thick hand-pressed masa cakes with pinched-up edges, griddled then fried and topped with refried beans, crumbled chorizo, potato, lettuce, and crema — a mercado stall classic.

ingredients.note: nixtamalised masa harina (Maseca brand) is carried by Mexican-goods importers and some supermarkets' international aisle; don't substitute rice flour or cornstarch
or use coarsely chopped longganiza with a pinch of cumin and a splash of vinegar if Mexican chorizo isn't available

ingredients.item: vegetable oil, for frying the sopes

ingredients.note: or lightly thinned sour cream
to taste

steps: Mix the masa harina with salt and warm water, kneading until a soft, crack-free dough forms; cover with a damp cloth.
Divide the dough into 8 balls and pat each into a thick disc about 8cm wide and 1cm thick.
Cook the discs on a hot dry griddle for 2-3 minutes per side until lightly speckled but not fully browned.
While still warm, pinch up the edge of each disc with your fingers to form a small raised wall, then set aside to cool slightly.
Crumble the chorizo into a skillet over medium heat and cook until rendered and browned, about 6-8 minutes, then stir in the diced potato.
Heat the oil in a wide skillet and fry each sope shell, wall-side up, for about 1 minute until the base crisps.
Spread each fried sope with refried beans, top with the chorizo-potato mixture, lettuce, queso fresco, and a drizzle of crema.
Serve immediately with salsa roja on the side.
tips: Keep the dough covered with a damp cloth while you work — masa dries out and cracks fast.
Pinch the walls while the disc is still warm; once it cools it won't hold the shape.
kidNote: Keep the salsa roja off the kids' sopes and pass it at the table so each person spoons on their own heat — the chorizo itself is only mildly spiced.
nutritionNote: A hearty combination of fried masa, pork, and cheese; balance with the shredded lettuce and go light on the crema.

title: Tlacoyos
description: Oval masa cakes stuffed with mashed beans, griddled until crisp-edged, and topped with nopales, cheese, and salsa — a central Mexican market breakfast staple.

ingredients.note: nixtamalised masa harina (Maseca brand) from a Mexican-goods importer; don't substitute plain cornstarch or rice flour

ingredients.item: cooked pinto or black beans, drained

ingredients.note: cactus is rarely available in Manila — substitute diced steamed green beans, or simply leave it out
to taste

steps: Heat the oil in a small pan, cook the garlic for 30 seconds, then add the beans and mash into a thick, spreadable paste; season with salt and let cool.
Mix the masa harina with salt and warm water, kneading until a soft dough forms that doesn't crack at the edges.
Divide the dough into 8 portions and flatten each into a small disc.
Place a spoonful of the mashed beans in the centre of each disc, fold the masa over the filling, and pinch closed.
Gently shape each stuffed ball into an oval about 1.5cm thick, patting to seal any cracks.
Cook on a hot dry griddle for 4-5 minutes per side until lightly charred and cooked through.
Top each tlacoyo with nopales, queso fresco, onion, and cilantro.
Serve with salsa verde on the side.
tips: Seal the edges well or the bean filling will burst out onto the griddle.
Tlacoyos freeze well after cooking; reheat straight from frozen on a dry pan.
nutritionNote: A fibre- and protein-rich vegetarian meal from the beans and corn masa; go easy on the cheese if serving as a main rather than a snack.

title: Fried Squash Blossom Quesadillas
localTitle: Quesadillas Fritas de Flor de Calabaza
description: Fresh squash blossoms and melting Oaxaca cheese folded into raw masa dough, then deep-fried to order — a market-stall quesadilla, unlike a griddled tortilla one.

ingredients.note: nixtamalised masa harina (Maseca brand); look for it at a Mexican-import grocer or order it online

ingredients.item: fresh squash blossoms, stems and pistils removed
ingredients.note: if unavailable, substitute finely sliced zucchini or kalabasa sauteed briefly with a little onion
or shredded mozzarella as the closest local substitute
epazote is hard to find locally — substitute a few chopped cilantro leaves
to taste

steps: Mix the masa harina with salt and warm water, kneading into a smooth dough that doesn't stick to your hands; cover with a damp cloth.
Roughly chop the squash blossoms and toss with the epazote.
Divide the masa into 8 balls and flatten each between two sheets of plastic into a thin round about 12cm wide.
Place a portion of cheese and squash blossoms on one half of each round, fold over, and press the edges firmly to seal.
Heat the oil in a deep skillet to about 175C, or until a small piece of dough sizzles immediately on contact.
Fry the quesadillas in batches for 2-3 minutes per side until deep golden and crisp.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot with salsa verde on the side.
tips: Seal the edges firmly — a loose seam lets the melting cheese leak into the oil.
Keep the oil at a steady medium-high heat; too hot browns the masa before the cheese melts through.
nutritionNote: Fried masa and melted cheese make this a rich treat rather than an everyday side; pair with a simple tomato or nopales salad.

title: Churros
description: Piped choux-style dough fried until crackly-crisp and rolled in cinnamon sugar, served with a cup of melted chocolate for dipping — the classic after-dark cart treat.

ingredients.note: plain flour, not self-rising

ingredients.item: chopped dark chocolate, for the dipping sauce
ingredients.note: a good local tablea or dark chocolate works well

steps: Combine the water, butter, salt, and cinnamon stick in a saucepan and bring to a boil.
Remove the cinnamon stick, take the pan off the heat, and stir in the flour all at once until a smooth dough forms.
Let the dough cool for 5 minutes, then beat in the egg until fully incorporated and glossy.
Spoon the dough into a piping bag fitted with a large star tip.
Heat the oil in a deep pan to about 175C and pipe 12cm lengths of dough directly into the oil, cutting with scissors.
Fry for 2-3 minutes per side until golden and crisp, then drain on paper towels.
Combine the sugar and ground cinnamon on a plate and roll the warm churros until coated.
Melt the chocolate gently and serve alongside the churros for dipping.
tips: Pipe straight into the oil rather than pre-shaping on a tray — it keeps the ridges crisp instead of flattening.
Work in small batches so the oil temperature doesn't drop and make the churros greasy.
nutritionNote: A fried-dough dessert high in sugar and fat; treat it as an occasional treat rather than an everyday snack.

title: Crispy Potato Tacos
description: Corn tortillas folded around spiced mashed potato and fried until crackly-edged — a meatless taco-stand favourite piled high with cabbage, cotija, and crema.

ingredients.note: use a mild paprika instead for a milder filling, and put hot sauce on the table separately
or finely crumbled salted white cheese
to taste

steps: Boil the potatoes in a large pot of salted water for 20-25 minutes until fork-tender, then drain.
Melt the butter in the same pot, add the garlic, and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Return the potatoes to the pot with the cumin, chili powder, and salt, and mash until smooth; taste and adjust seasoning.
Spread about 60g of the mashed potato onto one half of each tortilla and fold over to close.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and fry the tacos in batches, about 2 minutes per side, until golden and crisp.
Drain on paper towels.
Stuff or top the tacos with shredded cabbage, cotija cheese, and crema.
Serve with salsa or hot sauce passed separately at the table.
tips: Warm the tortillas briefly before folding so they don't crack.
The mashed filling can be made up to 3 days ahead and refrigerated, then fried fresh.
nutritionNote: A meatless, filling option that's heavy on fried starch; balance with the shredded cabbage and a squeeze of lime rather than extra crema.

title: Molletes
description: Split bread rolls spread with refried beans and melted cheese, broiled until bubbling — Mexico's everyday cafeteria breakfast or afternoon snack.

ingredients.item: bolillo rolls or other crusty white rolls
ingredients.note: pandesal or a small split baguette are good Manila substitutes
or shredded mozzarella
to taste

steps: Preheat the broiler and cut the rolls in half lengthwise.
Scoop out a little of the soft crumb from the centre of each half to make room for the filling.
Spread the cut sides with butter and broil for 3-4 minutes until lightly golden.
Remove from the broiler and spread each half generously with warm refried beans.
Top with the shredded cheese and return to the broiler for 3-5 minutes until melted and bubbling.
Top with pico de gallo and serve with avocado slices on the side.
tips: Warm the beans before spreading so the broiler only needs to melt the cheese, not heat the whole thing through.
Watch the broiler closely in the last minute — cheese can go from melted to burnt fast.
nutritionNote: A balanced breakfast from the beans' fibre and protein and the bread's carbohydrates; the avocado adds healthy fat in place of extra cheese.
